english.html: of St John, said that he was Elijah g, whom the Lord God had promised by the Prophet h: not, says St Augustine, that Jesus understood St John to be the very person of Elijah, but by imitation of virtue i. Otherwise, whoever changes his name must be punished and repressed by the penalty of forgery x, and such a one (said the Jurisconsult Ulpian in some place) that he may be an example to others l [unclear: the print reads & telle, (diſoit en quelque lieu le Iuriſconſulte Vlpien qu'il en ſoit) autres aux exemple, with the parenthesis closed too late and autres aux inverted; translated by the evident sense].

notes.gloss: "This is Elias, which was for to come."
"Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet."

notes.citation: Decretum of Gratian, Part II, C. 22 q. 2, c. Quaeritur (Augustine; cf. C. 22 q. 2 c. 22)
notes.gloss: Augustine on figurative speech that is not a lie — John called Elijah by likeness of spirit, not identity of person. Cited again at annot-081 {g} for Jacob.

notes.citation: Digest 48.10 (De lege Cornelia de falsis), l. Falsi (D. 48.10.13 pr., Papinian)
notes.gloss: The assertion of a false name or cognomen is punished with the penalty of falsum — the text Coras's whole annotation rests on; cited also at annot-012 {c}. The margin keys this note x, as the body marker is read; the alphabet expects k.

notes.gloss: Cited again, with the same abbreviation, at annot-081 {a} for exemplary punishment; the Ulpian saying Coras paraphrases, that the penalty should be an example to others, has not been located under this title.

english.html: Arnauld du Tilh had substituted upon himself the name and person of Martin Guerre, and so subtly laid so many snares to bait and keep everyone in the persuasion of such an imposture, that the said de Rols, his wife, the sisters, the uncle and the kinsfolk of the same Martin were lulled in it for three years and more: a notable substitution certainly, if ever one was discovered, and worthy of atrocious, cruel and exemplary punishment <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>, although of this crime our laws and canons have spoken so sparingly, and so rarely, that there is found no text which can properly belong to this case. It is true that Modestinus, speaking of him who, not being a soldier, nevertheless calls and maintains himself to be such, or who uses forbidden insignia and arms, or indeed forges false letters of the Prince, wills and ordains that he be most grievously punished <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>. Pope Clement III also makes mention of a priest who had taken the name and title of a King's son, and under this cloak taken up arms and stirred up a great sedition: of the penalty he says not a single word <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>. Mention is also made of I know not what Barbarius Philippus, a slave, who presented himself to the Roman people as a free person, and as such carried off the dignity of Praetor; but whether he did well or ill, the Jurisconsult does not open his mouth with a single word <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>. Everyone knows also that mention is made in our law of the substitution of children <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup>. But what! these are all crimes diverse and separate from this one; and it would certainly not be easy to give certain rules upon the penalty: as much because our laws have determined nothing about it, as also because the ancients have

notes.citation: Digest, title abbreviated de reb. cor. — not resolved; the fragment beginning Quamvis not identified
notes.original: l. quamuis D. de reb. cor.
notes.gloss: As at annot-080 {l}, for exemplary punishment.

notes.citation: Digest 48.10 (De lege Cornelia de falsis), l. Eos qui, last paragraph (D. 48.10.27.2, Modestinus)
notes.original: l. eos. P fin. D. de falſi..
notes.gloss: He who has passed himself off as a soldier, or used unlawful insignia, or travelled with a forged warrant (falso diplomate), is to be punished most severely according to the nature of the offence — the three cases Coras lists.

notes.citation: Decretals of Gregory IX, title De sententia excommunicationis (X 5.39), c. Perpendimus (Clement III; chapter number unverified)
notes.original: c. perpendi mus. de ſent. excom.
notes.gloss: The priest who claimed to be a king's son and raised a sedition; cited again at {m}.

notes.citation: Digest 1.14 (De officio praetorum), l. Barbarius (D. 1.14.3, Ulpian; Coras's l. 2 by the older numbering)
notes.original: l. ij. D. offi. prætor. de
notes.gloss: Barbarius Philippus, a runaway slave, held the praetorship at Rome; his acts were held valid — Ulpian says nothing of his punishment.

notes.citation: Digest 37.10 (De Carboniano edicto), l. 1, last paragraph, and l. 2; Code 9.22 (Ad legem Corneliam de falsis), l. 1 (C. 9.22.1)
notes.original: l. i. P. fi. & l. ij. D. de Ca. bo. edic. l. i. C. de fal.
notes.gloss: The Carbonian edict governs disputes over a child alleged to be supposititious; the Code law, the "law of Antoninus" of {a} on p118, on the substitution of a child.

lines: de S. Iean diſoit, que c'eſtoit Elie {g}, que le Seigneur
Dieu auoit promis par le Prophe {h}. non point dit S.
Auguſtin, que Ieſus entendit S. Iean eſtre la meſme per
ſonne d'Elie: mais par imitation de vertu {i}. Autrement,
qui change de nom, doit eſtre puni & reprimé par pei
ne de faux {x}. & telle, (diſoit en quelque lieu le Iuriſcon-
ſulte Vlpien qu'il en ſoit) autres aux exemple {l}.
Arnauld du Tilh auoit ſuppoſé le nom & la perſonne
de Martin Guerre, & ſi ſubtilement tendu tant de la-
çons pour appaſter, & entretenir chacun à la perſuaſiõ
de telle impoſture, que leſdits de Rols femme, ſeurs,
oncle, & parens d'iceluy Martin, y furẽt endormis trois
ans & d'auantage: ſuppoſition notable certes, ſ'il en fut
oncques deſcouuerte, & digne d'atroce, cuelle, & exem
plaire punition {a}, bien que de ce crime, noz loix, & ca-
nons, ayent fort ſobrement, & ſi rarement parlé, qu'il
ne ſe trouue aucun texte qui puiſſe proprement apparte
nir à ce fait. Il eſt vray, que Modeſtin parlant de celuy
lequel n'eſtant point ſoldat, neantmoins ſe dit & main
tient pour tel: ou qui vſe d'enſeignes & armoiries de-
fenduës, on bien ſuppoſe fauſſes lettres du Prince, veut
& ordonne qu'il ſoit treſgriefuement puni {b}. Le Pape
Clement iij, auſſi fait mention d'vn preſtre qui auoit
prins le nom, & le titre de fils de Roy, & ſous ce man-
teau, prins les armes, & excité vne grande ſedition: de la
peine, n'en dit pas vn ſeul mot {c}. Il eſt auſſi parlé de ie ne
ſçay quel Barbare Philippe ſerf, qui ſe preſenta au peu
ple Romain, comme vne perſonne franche, & comme
telle en rapporta la dignité de Preteur. mais ſ'il fit
bien ou mal, le Iuriſconſulte n'en ouure pas vne ſeule
parole {d}. Chacun ſçait auſſi, qu'il eſt fait mention en
noſtre droit, de la ſuppoſition des enfans {e}. Mais quoy?
ce ſont tous crimes diuers, & ſeparez de ceſtuy-ci.
& ne ſeroit certainement aiſé donner certaines reigles
ſur la peine: tant par ce que noz loix n'en ont rien de
terminé, que pour autant auſſi, que les anciens ont
